name: Cairo 0
typeSystem: Minimal and low-level: Cairo 0 source has static compiler-level constructs such as felt values, pointers, tuples, and structs, while Cairo VM memory ultimately stores field elements in write-once cells. It is closer to an assembly language for a zero-knowledge-friendly CPU than a general-purpose language.
runtime: Cairo 0 programs compile to Cairo assembly executed by the Cairo VM, producing an execution trace that a separate STARK prover turns into a succinct, verifiable proof.

runtimes.name: Cairo VM (CairoZero)
runtimes.role: Executes compiled Cairo 0 programs, producing an execution trace consumed by a STARK prover.

compilers.name: cairo-compile (Cairo 0)
compilers.role: Compiles Cairo 0 source to Cairo assembly/bytecode for the Cairo VM.

concurrencyModel: N/A (single deterministic execution trace, later proved and verified; no concurrency).
